title: Minimum Squares for PSD Polynomials (Pfister Bound)
description: Investigates the minimum number of squares of rational functions needed to represent PSD polynomials. Proves Brahmagupta-Fibonacci closure (product of 2-SOS is 2-SOS), SOS monotonicity, PSD characterization, and concrete examples. Fully verified: 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

SOS monotonicity: k-SOS implies m-SOS for m ≥ k
Concrete witnesses: x², x²+1, (x²+1)² as SOS with explicit decompositions
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 17th problem (1900) asked whether every nonneg polynomial can be expressed as a sum of squares of rational functions. Hilbert himself (1888) proved that not every nonneg polynomial is a sum of polynomial squares: the Motzkin polynomial M(x,y) = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ - 3x²y² + 1 is nonneg but not polynomial-SOS. Artin resolved the problem (1927): every PSD polynomial over a real closed field is a sum of squares of rational functions. The quantitative question — how many rational squares are needed — was settled by Pfister (1967): any PSD polynomial in n variables is a sum of at most 2^n squares of rational functions, and this bound is tight (Cassels-Ellison-Pfister 1971 showed no bound smaller than 2^n works for general n-variate polynomials). The bound 2^n comes from Pfister forms: n-fold tensor products of the identity (a²+b²)(c²+d²) = (ac-bd)² + (ad+bc)² (Brahmagupta-Fibonacci). This identity itself goes back to Brahmagupta (628 CE) in the context of Pell equations and was rediscovered by Fibonacci (1225). The algebraic structure behind it is norm multiplicativity of Gaussian integers: |z₁z₂|² = |z₁|²|z₂|², where |a+bi|² = a²+b². The extension to 4 squares uses quaternion norms (Euler's 4-square identity, 1748), and to 8 squares uses octonions (Cayley-Dickson), explaining why 2^n is exactly the right bound.
overview.problemStatement:
Given Pfister's general bound of $2^n$ squares for PSD polynomials in $n$ variables, what is the minimum number of squares needed for specific classes?

**Known results**:
- Univariate: 2 squares suffice (closure under multiplication via Brahmagupta-Fibonacci)
- Bivariate quartics: polynomial-SOS (Hilbert 1888)
- General: $2^n$ is optimal (Pfister forms)

We formalize the algebraic infrastructure and prove key structural results.
overview.text: Investigates the minimum number of squares of rational functions needed to represent PSD polynomials, proving Brahmagupta-Fibonacci closure and structural results.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Define IsPSD, IsSumOfKSquares, IsSOS for univariate polynomials
2. Prove the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity: (a²+b²)(c²+d²) = (ac-bd)² + (ad+bc)²
3. Use this to show: product of two 2-SOS polynomials is 2-SOS
4. Prove SOS monotonicity and soundness (SOS → PSD)
5. Give explicit SOS witnesses for x², x²+1, (x²+1)²
keyInsights: The Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity (628 CE → 1225 CE → 1967) is the algebraic engine: (a²+b²)(c²+d²) = (ac-bd)² + (ad+bc)² proves 2-SOS polynomials are closed under multiplication. Proved in Lean by ring — one line!

The identity has a profound interpretation: it is norm multiplicativity of Gaussian integers, |z₁z₂|² = |z₁|²|z₂|². This generalizes to 4 squares via quaternion norms (Euler 1748) and 8 squares via octonions — explaining why Pfister's bound is exactly 2^n
SOS monotonicity (k-SOS → m-SOS) follows by padding with 0² terms via Fin.cons 0. The proof is by induction on Nat.le, adding one zero summand per step
IsSumOfKSquares uses Fin k → Polynomial ℝ for the witnesses, making it compatible with BigOperators (∑ i, q i ^ 2) and enabling Finset.sum_nonneg for the soundness proof

The hard direction — PSD implies rational-SOS — is Artin's theorem (1927), not proved here. The Lean formalization captures the algebraic infrastructure (definitions, monotonicity, product closure) that is needed before tackling Artin
x²+1 = x² + 1² is explicitly 2-SOS; (x²+1)² is 1-SOS since it equals (x²+1)². These witnesses demonstrate that the SOS number can decrease when taking powers

sections.title: SOS Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsPSD (nonneg for all inputs), IsSumOfKSquares (sum of exactly k polynomial squares), IsSOS (sum of some number of squares).
sections.mathContext: A polynomial $p$ is PSD if $p(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. It is $k$-SOS if $p = \sum_{i=1}^k q_i^2$.

sections.title: Basic SOS Results
sections.summary: Proves concrete examples (x², x²+1), PSD addition closure, SOS implies PSD, and SOS monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: If $p = \sum q_i^2$ then $p(x) = \sum q_i(x)^2 \geq 0$. If $p$ is $k$-SOS then it is $m$-SOS for any $m \geq k$ by adding $0^2$ terms.

sections.title: Brahmagupta-Fibonacci Identity
sections.summary: Proves the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity for reals and polynomials, then uses it to show 2-SOS is closed under multiplication.
sections.mathContext: $(a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2) = (ac-bd)^2 + (ad+bc)^2$. This is the norm multiplicativity of Gaussian integers: $|z_1 z_2|^2 = |z_1|^2 |z_2|^2$.

sections.title: Pfister Bound Structure
sections.summary: Records Pfister bound values 2^n for small n and proves monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: Pfister's theorem: $2^n$ squares suffice for $n$-variate PSD polynomials. Values: $2, 4, 8$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$.

conclusion.summary: Fully verified formalization (0 axioms, 0 sorries) of the algebraic infrastructure for Pfister's bound optimization. The Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity provides the multiplicative closure that explains why 2 squares suffice in the univariate case.
conclusion.implications: The Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity generalizes to higher Pfister forms (4-square identity of Euler, 8-square identity of Cayley-Dickson), explaining the power-of-2 structure in Pfister's bound. This formalization provides the foundation for a complete treatment.

mainTheorems.name: two_sos_closed_under_mul
mainTheorems.description: Product closure: the product of two 2-SOS polynomials is again 2-SOS, proved via the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity (a²+b²)(c²+d²) = (ac-bd)² + (ad+bc)² — one line of ring in Lean.

mainTheorems.name: brahmagupta_fibonacci_poly
mainTheorems.description: The Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity in polynomial form: (p²+q²)(r²+s²) = (pr-qs)² + (ps+qr)², the algebraic engine explaining why 2 squares suffice for univariate PSD polynomials.

mainTheorems.name: sos_monotone
mainTheorems.description: SOS monotonicity: if p is k-SOS then p is m-SOS for any m ≥ k, proved by padding with 0² terms via Fin.cons 0 and induction on Nat.le.
